writeup.headline: Tidewater rates Hold: strong balance sheet and margins offset by flat revenue and lagging recent returns.
writeup.thesis: Tidewater scores 60, a Hold, 5 points short of the Buy band. The balance sheet is the standout (score 89), with net debt at 0.15 times free cash flow and cash covering 0.94 of debt. Quality is solid at 72, with a 48.4% gross margin, an 18.4% operating margin, a 20.1% free cash flow margin and diluted share count up 0.2% year on year. Growth is the main drag at 34: a TTM revenue decline of 1.0% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 0.2% year on year, though growth sped up by 2.4 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 66 on moderate absolute levels (3.2x sales, 15.9x free cash flow, 17.5x EV/EBIT, FCF yield 1.3 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield), and P/S sits near the middle of its own history; trend is mixed at 61, and news is neutral.
key_risks: Revenue is flat to slightly down, with a TTM revenue decline of 1.0%, so earnings depend on day rates holding up.
Integrating the WSUT acquisition and delivering revised 2026 guidance of $1.42 to $1.47 billion revenue and a 49% to 50% gross margin.
About $13.1 million of expected Middle East conflict-related costs in 2026, with the risk of more.
Shares 11.1 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and price 14.0% below its 52-week high, showing fading momentum.
Offshore vessel demand is cyclical and tied to energy spending, and competitors are consolidating.
what_would_change: A 5-point gain would reach Buy, most plausibly from a better growth score if Q3 results show revenue growth returning with the WSUT contribution.
Renewed relative strength, with the price back above its 50-day average, would lift the trend score.
A 16-point drop would be needed for Sell, for example a guidance cut, margin compression or a sharp share price decline hitting several factors together.
Negative news on guidance, customers or insider selling would pull the neutral news score lower.
